pageTitle: MP4Flow — Free MP4 Video Converter for Mac
pageDescription: Convert MOV, MKV and AVI to MP4 on Mac. Batch convert, merge and edit videos locally. Free and open source, for Apple silicon and Intel.
socialImageAlt: MP4Flow, a native Mac video converter, showing its real English crop window with Tears of Steel
installIntro: Homebrew installs both tools MP4Flow needs: FFmpeg and ffprobe.
installStepThree: In MP4Flow, select Environment Check → Recheck.
installHelp: No Homebrew? Install it first and complete its Next steps:
aspectBody: Fix stretched or squashed video without cropping away the picture.
editorGuide: Open Edit Video in the queue. Brightness and denoise are in Image Adjustments. Apply your edits, then start conversion.
adjustNote: Image adjustments require re-encoding and do not support HDR. Light denoise is off by default and may slightly soften detail.
mergeBody: Join unedited clips in queue order. Merge directly when compatible, or use Compatible Merge to match formats.
brightenBody: Adjust brightness and gently lift shadows. Preview the result as you edit.
denoiseBody: Reduce visible grain in dark scenes. Enable a light touch of noise reduction when needed.
heroFormats: MOV, MKV, AVI and WMV to MP4
faqFormatsQ: Can I convert MOV, MKV or AVI to MP4 on a Mac?
faqFormatsA: MP4Flow converts common MOV, MKV, AVI and WMV videos to MP4. Support depends on the codecs in the file and your installed FFmpeg build.
faqPrivacyQ: Is MP4Flow free? Do I need to upload my videos?
faqPrivacyA: MP4Flow is free and open source. Videos are processed on your Mac, with no account or video uploads required.
faqQualityQ: Will converting a video make the file smaller?
faqQualityA: Not always. Smart Convert can copy compatible video without re-encoding. Set a target size in Export Settings, or lower the resolution. Size is approximate; re-encoding may reduce quality.
faqSetupQ: What do I need to get started?
faqSetupA: Use macOS 13+ on Apple silicon or Intel. Drag MP4Flow from the DMG to Applications, then install FFmpeg and ffprobe separately. The guide includes Homebrew steps.
exportBody: Set a target size, choose audio tracks, and keep or burn text subtitles.
recoveryBody: Keep your queue and settings between launches. Restart unfinished tasks when you’re ready.
exportNote: Target size is an estimate; compression may reduce quality. Burning text subtitles requires FFmpeg with libass.
installOptionalBody: For this feature, install an FFmpeg build with libass:
tourTrimBody: Drag the range or enter exact start and end times. Preview the part you want to keep.
tourCropBody: Pick a shape, drag the selection, or enter exact crop dimensions.
tourAspectBody: Fix stretched proportions with presets or a custom ratio, with live preview and no extra crop.
tourAdjustBody: Gently lift shadows, compare with the original, and enable light denoise when needed.
tourExportBody: Set an approximate size, choose audio, and keep or burn a text-subtitle track.
